description: Precompile candidate witness scaffolds into abelian networks with explicit sink placements and use odometer profiles to predict which regions are close to certifiable collapse into T. The distinctive search variable is sink geometry on the product grid and how it concentrates certificate pressure.
mathematical_formalization: A compiler \mathcal{C} sends a scaffold H to an abelian network A(H,s) with sink set s. Let u_s(v) be the resulting odometer. Search sink placements and local label templates that maximize \mathrm{Corr}(u_s(v),1_{v\in T_\infty}) while minimizing decoded score S.
analogical_connections: Forcing pressure as sandpile odometer height.
Local linear span as abelian stabilization.
implementation_hypothesis: For each small scaffold, build the abelian network once, sweep sink placements and local labels, benchmark odometer features against depth and degree baselines, and use winning sink geometries to initialize R or glue edges.
experiment_seed: Benchmark 100-500 small scaffolds with matched depth/degree controls and label-shuffled variants. Stop immediately if odometer features do not outperform trivial graph baselines.

closest_prior_art.title: Abelian Networks I. Foundations and Examples
Integral Flow and Cycle Chip-Firing on Graphs
Bounds on arithmetic projections, and applications to the Kakeya conjecture

novelty_claim: This turns sink placement into a tunable compiler parameter for exact arithmetic forcing rather than treating abelian dynamics as a loose analogy.
differentiation: The invariant is used only to choose arithmetic witness geometry and seeds; the abelian network itself is not the target object.
